_comment: Shared MCP handshake corpus. Replayed by lib/core/tests/Unit/Domain/Mcp/McpHandshakeCorpusTest.php and by the WordPress-side addons/pro/tests/test-mcp-handshake-policy-parity.php, so the core policy and its WordPress adapter are held to one contract. Each case is a failed handshake: http_status 0 means the transport itself failed. rpc_code null means the body carried no JSON-RPC error envelope, which is the strict-gateway shape.

cases.name: strict-gateway-bare-400
cases.note: Upwork-style gateway answers an unknown probe method with no JSON-RPC envelope. The status alone has to count.

cases.name: jsonrpc-invalid-request
cases.note: Some 2025-era servers answer an unknown method with -32600 rather than -32601.

cases.name: session-header-required
cases.note: The decisive asymmetry: a session complaint proves legacy and must never be read as a stateless signal.

cases.name: session-message-on-http-200
cases.note: A 200 carrying a session complaint is still a legacy server.

cases.name: gateway-404
cases.note: Endpoint-level rejection of the probe path.

cases.name: gateway-405
cases.note: The probe method is not allowed; the dialect is legacy.

cases.name: server-error-500
cases.note: No dialect signal: keep the cached hint and surface the error.

cases.name: auth-401
cases.note: Credentials problem, not a dialect problem.

cases.name: forbidden-403
cases.note: Scope problem, not a dialect problem.

cases.name: rate-limited-429
cases.note: Must not be mistaken for a dialect rejection, or a throttled server would be re-probed with initialize.

cases.name: transport-timeout
cases.message: cURL error 28: Operation timed out after 10000 milliseconds
cases.note: No response at all. A timeout is not evidence of a dialect.

cases.name: success-shaped-empty
cases.note: Pins that a clean 200 never classifies as a rejection.
